description:
Found while reviewing fz-3ul.3 against the BEAM. The handler miss (a try whose rescue/catch clauses all miss) and the after handler re-raise by calling Kernel.raise_kind/2, resolved by name through the calling module's namespace (body.rs reraise_block -> call_raising_block). That forces raise_kind/2 to be public auto-imported Kernel surface Elixir does not have, and because it takes a kind atom from anyone, fz_raise_kind parses the atom (RaiseKind::from_name) and invents a :badarg error for an unknown kind.

The BEAM has the same primitive but not the same door: erlang:throw/1, erlang:exit/1 and erlang:error/1,2 are fixed-class BIFs behind Kernel's throw/exit/raise; the try handler is a case over {Class, Value, RawStk} whose fallthrough is the compiler primop raise(RawStk, Value), which hands back exactly what the landing pad delivered. Nothing in Kernel takes a class; erlang:raise/3 lives in the runtime's module.

Build: the handler miss and the after re-raise become a terminator in the Term::Raise family (a LastResort variant that continues the arrived raise with the handler's delivered kind and value), emitted by native codegen and the interpreter directly to the runtime's private raise route, with the kind as the runtime delivered it (no atom round trip). throw/1 and exit/1 call fixed-kind externs the way raise/2 calls fz_raise. Delete Kernel.raise_kind/2 (def, @doc, @spec, the lib/runtime.fz entry, the kernel.fz module doc mention), extern fz_raise_kind, RaiseKind::from_name and the :badarg branch, reraise_block's DirectCall and call_raising_block if it loses its last user. reraise/2 stays panic(exception) until fz-3ul.5 gives it a stacktrace to carry.

Acceptance (interp, run, build):
- fixtures 00733-00739, 00750-00757, 00758-00793 pass unchanged; in particular the catch fixtures (a throw that no clause takes reaches the outer catch as a throw; exit(:normal)/exit(:shutdown)/exit({:shutdown, n}) through a try ... after end main with status 0/0/n; an uncaught throw prints ** (throw) v, exit 1).
- grep -rn 'raise_kind' lib src runtime .agent is empty.
- a program calling raise_kind(:throw, 1) is the ordinary undefined-function diagnostic.
- fz.runtime.raise telemetry for a re-raise through an after is unchanged: two events, the re-raise one frame shallower, same kind on both.
- unit tests: the runtime's kind-carrying entry rejects nothing because it accepts no atom (the test for :badarg is deleted with the branch); the lowering test for the handler miss asserts the terminator, not a call.
- .agent/docs/exceptions.md (kinds table, 'throw/1, exit/1 and raise_kind/2 are plain fz code' paragraph, handler-miss and after bullets, 'Where it lives'), runtime-telemetry.md line ~92, lib/kernel.fz docs updated in the same commit; no pin or golden moves.
- gate green as in the epic.
title: The handler miss re-raises as a terminator, and raise_kind/2 leaves Kernel
